leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations contain a single prize part, B017 (GLP-1 physiology and incretin therapies), with the identical trio Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Linnarsson and Wahren-Herlenius moved from opening ballots that included Knudsen to this trio. Citations differ only in wording: three centre on the incretin hormone GLP-1 and its active form (El Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg), and three on the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form (Linnarsson, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius). Shared: B017 is mature, original and independently confirmed, and credit is its weakest point. Not shared: how much weight the Knudsen omission and the drug-design step deserve. No member's configuration includes a second prize part. Alternatives are B006 (named by all six), B024 (El Manira, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson), B049 (Linnarsson) and B018 (Wahren-Herlenius); none of these is a configuration preference.

areas_of_agreement: All six members put B017 as the sole prize part with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and all six list B006 (CAR-T) among their alternatives.

All six describe B017 as a continuous chain from gut-hormone physiology and the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide to drugs with randomized outcome evidence in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints, and as mature and independently confirmed.
All six name attribution as the main weakness of B017, specifically the contested priority for the active peptide form (Mojsov versus Habener and others) and the omission of Knudsen.
Members state that unanimous opening support for B017 is not itself an argument for merit.
scientific_disputes: Whether the citation should reward the physiological discovery of the hormone and its active form only, or also acknowledge the long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide). Members write that the physiology-centred framing is defensible but leaves a visible gap.

Weight given to the central appetite effects of GLP-1: El Manira cites them as part of the case, while the chair's round-1 file leans on gut-pancreas physiology and the outcome data, with the CNS mechanism still being worked out.

Whether B017 should stand as a single achievement or be paired with a second part (B006, B024 or B018). Members note this either strengthens the award or dilutes a near-unanimous first choice, and no one has argued for a specific pairing.
attribution_disputes: Mojsov versus Habener and other early investigators for identification of the active GLP-1 peptide and its insulinotropic role. Several members state that they have not verified this priority from the supplied evidence.

Mojsov versus Knudsen for the third seat. All six now choose Mojsov, but Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius each call the Knudsen omission a real cost, and Linnarsson calls it a close call.

For alternatives, B006 lacks Eshhar among the supplied names and Sandberg limits it to June and Sadelain without Rosenberg. B024 lacks Rowley for upstream BCR-ABL work. B049 has six credited names against a three-person limit, as Linnarsson notes.
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B017. The maturity questions concern alternatives only: whether B006 and B024 are comparable in maturity and attribution completeness to B017, and whether B024 is better seen as drug development than as discovery (Perlmann).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) discloses about twenty co-authored works with Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy) and a postdoctoral period with Greengard. Neither bears on a shortlisted candidate.
Perlmann notes past co-authorship with Svenningsson and El Manira, and ties to Ronald Evans and Johan Ericson. None involves a shortlisted candidate.
El Manira discloses ties to Grillner and Ernfors and a 2009 paper with Perlmann. He notes that B049 (optogenetics) touches his field, but he does not propose it.
Sandberg discloses eight joint works with Linnarsson and co-authorship with Frisén. None involves a shortlisted candidate.
Wahren-Herlenius flags topical proximity of her field to B018 (anti-TNF) and to CAR-T in autoimmune disease, but documents no collaboration with any credited name.
Linnarsson reports no specific conflict. No member requests recusal from any ballot ID.
questions_for_round2: Should the third B017 seat go to Mojsov (identification of the active peptide) or Knudsen (design of long-acting analogues), and can the citation wording make the omission a stated principle rather than an oversight?
Can the Mojsov versus Habener priority question for the active GLP-1 peptide be resolved from the supplied evidence, and if not, how should it affect the credited names or the citation?

Should B017 stand alone, or does a second prize part strengthen the award? If so, which of B006 (CAR-T, with or without Rosenberg and without Eshhar), B024 (BCR-ABL, without Rowley) or B018 (anti-TNF) has a defensible attribution within the three-person limit per prize?
Does the committee want a physiology-centred citation (hormone and active form) or one that also covers therapeutic development, and how much weight should central appetite effects receive?
Should the absence of Eshhar from B006 and of Rowley from B024 exclude those candidates as second parts, or can their citations be narrowed to a defensible contribution?
summary.chair_observation: The six round-1 files agree on B017 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and the only recorded alternatives are B006 (all six), B024 (four members), B049 (one) and B018 (one). Agreement on the first part is complete. Round 2 therefore mainly needs to settle the third seat and the citation wording for B017, and to decide whether any second part has a defensible attribution. The files contain no explicit votes for any second prize part.
